ani: Reused existing canonical prayer:amidah/qedushah/ani, parallel to the established qadosh/barukh parts; no new prayer identity. Existing registry also contains ani_hashem_elohaykhem. This edition chooses the existing shared qedushah/ani vocabulary. Source remains Numbers15:41b. No duplicate Bible half-verse owner is minted. Word home has no speaker; source/expanded occurrences supply exactly one role. English uses contextual lexical quotation milestones, not accentual half-verses.
ranges: Vetimlokh prayer-part and Psalm146:10 now have separate canonical pointers and the prayer-part terminates before the Psalm. No cross-namespace range.
inner_rite_declarations: Not needed here: plain canonical word homes contain no rite conditions, and no downstream variant/dependency derives a custom from these local wrappers. The wrappers evaluate the existing outer rite setting directly. Adding an identical local declaration would not resolve an unknown conditional and would add no behavior. Keep actual rite declaration scopes used by older settings-dependent passages unchanged.
source_newlines: Raw source linefeed is preserved as protected literal evidence; normalized generated XML collapses it to whitespace, with no lb/p/l created for it.
isaiah_part: opensiddur/common/subverse.py declares Isaiah6:3/veqara and /qadosh; the Kesod quote stops at the existing qadosh remainder. Context path normalized to quotations/isaiah_6/3.
identity_search: normalized-identity-search.json covers complete current registry labels and actual existing project bodies. Existing Adir /addir hit is siddur:regalim/musaf/text/addir (entire edition occurrence), not prayer:amidah/addir_adiraynu/addir. The canonical root existed, but no old canonical subpart of different extent exists. Tisgav has no previous registry/corpus identity (the only registry hit is this uncommitted new record).
fuerth: Fuerth true plus Frankfurt/Metz false decides inclusion; Fuerth true with other customs unknown leaves inclusion labelled unresolved, preserving the three-valued rite model.
